issues.description: The solution implements a function named write_pixel but the template and problem statement expect a function named set_pixel. Main (both template and solution main) calls set_pixel, but the solution does not define set_pixel (only write_pixel). This name/signature mismatch will cause confusion and a linkage/undefined-symbol error, preventing students from running or comparing the solution with the provided template and instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's function name match the template/problem expectation: either rename write_pixel to set_pixel in the solution, or change the call site in main to call write_pixel. Ensure the function signature and register usage follow the problem specification (x in EAX, y in EBX, color in ECX) and preserves other registers as required.

issues.description: The problem statement and template explicitly refer to a subroutine named 'set_pixel' that students must implement. In the provided solution the pixel-writing routine is implemented under the label 'write_pixel' (solution_repository/pixel.asm lines 19-34) while main still invokes 'set_pixel' (solution_repository/pixel.asm line 147). This creates a naming mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the routine that writes a pixel) and will confuse students mapping the requirement 'implement set_pixel' to the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the routine name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'write_pixel' label to 'set_pixel' (or change the call sites to 'write_pixel') so the subroutine that writes a pixel uses the same identifier as the problem statement and template.
